analysis:
This batch shows the wiring for a new add-on hold feature. The implementation files are not supplied: ProviderLoop+AddonHold, AddonIPCServer, AddonHoldBook, AddonHoldPaths and ProviderDrain.refusingForServiceChange/owner.

Changes examined:
(1) ProviderLoop.swift head 484-497 adds add-on hold state. It includes a local IPC socket server (addonIPCServer), a peer authenticator override seam (addonPeerAuthenticatorOverride), a lease monitor and a drain timeout. This is new local attack surface not covered by any TB in the threat model. A local process, possibly operator-controlled, can request holds that drain and unload models. That is an availability effect within ADV-001's existing control of their own Mac. It is analogous to TB-010/T-044, the fan helper peer impersonation threat. Peer authentication, socket path permissions and the test-seam override must be verified in the unsupplied AddonIPCServer source. Integration should confirm the override cannot be set in production builds.
(2) StartupPreload.swift head 195-197 only logs when owner == .addonHold. The existing guard at line 198 (!servingDrain.refusing) still returns .cancelled, so a hold suppresses preload and registration. That is fail-safe.
(3) StartupShutdown.swift head 27 changes the condition from !refusing to !refusingForServiceChange. A stop now begins a lifecycle drain even while an add-on hold owns the drain. Shutdown still sets isShuttingDown and stops the endpoint, preload, AppAttest worker and inflight work. No weakening of teardown is visible. The precise semantics of refusingForServiceChange are unverified.
(4) Trust.swift head 108 adds addonHold: addonHoldSnapshot to the daemon state file. Integration should verify the snapshot contains no secrets, peer identities or tokens (T-058-style diagnostic leakage), and that state-file permissions are unchanged.

No consumer prompt (A-001), key (A-003) or authorization (A-016) path changes are visible here. The threat model likely needs a new boundary entry for the add-on IPC.
